category_feedback.specific_evidence: input_row.json defines A8.4 as 'describe how likely familiar events are to happen' (probability/likelihood), but lesson_04 and the blueprint redefine A8.4 as 'describe and interpret simple data displays' (most/fewest/equal). The lesson teaches graph-reading vocabulary (most, fewest, same) — none of which addresses likelihood of familiar events. The curriculum_expectations text is not byte-identical to the source row; it is a substantive substitution. This drifts the entire pair away from its planned code.
category_feedback.required_fix: Either (a) re-target lesson_04 to A8.4 as written in input_row.json — likelihood language for familiar events (will it rain today? always/sometimes/never; more likely/less likely with concrete K examples like 'will the sun set tonight?' vs 'will it snow in July?') — OR (b) raise this discrepancy to the blueprint owner and have the input_row corrected upstream before the pair re-runs. Until the lesson's primary_expectations match the verbatim curriculum text in input_row.json, this pair cannot pass.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: duration_minutes: 50 with minds_on 12 / action 25 / consolidation 13. The rubric specifies K time allocation as 30-40 min; this lesson runs 50 min — the same window as G2-G3. A 5-year-old carpet block of 12 min plus a 25 min three-station rotation (7 min each) plus a 13 min consolidation will exceed Kindergarten attention span and collide with snack/recess on a real schedule. There is also no no-paper, no-purchase alternative path called out anywhere in differentiation; the for_movement_learners 'human bar graph' is close but is positioned as enrichment, not as a runnable substitute when the pictographs aren't prepped.
category_feedback.required_fix: Tighten total duration to 30-40 min for K (suggest 8 minds_on / 18 action / 8 consolidation = 34 min; cut to two stations of 8 min each, or whole-group only). Promote the human-bar-graph movement variant into an explicit no-paper alternative: 'No-prep version — children line up by attribute (shoe colour, lunch type), teacher and class compare line lengths by walking from end to end and counting. Same most/fewest/same questions, no pictographs needed.'
